summary: The note surveys fundraising ideas that amateur sports teams used in the 2023 season to cover rising costs of equipment, travel and facilities. It covers tech-driven approaches (crowdfunding, tokens), modernized traditional events, corporate sponsorships, merchandise, Grow-A-Thon plant sales, VIP packages, clinics, fantasy games, online bake sales and in-game donations. Each idea is illustrated with a named team and leader, and the note concludes that the future lies in merging technology, community engagement and sustainable partnerships.
one_line: Overview of innovative 2023 fundraising strategies used by amateur sports teams, each illustrated with a named team example.
key_facts: The Jefferson City Jaguars, led by Coach Mary Simmons, held a 24-hour digital donation marathon on October 15th that raised upwards of $10,000.
The Capital Heights Rowing Club is pioneering a 'token economy' of tradable digital tokens, spearheaded by financial officer Laura Green, with proceeds funding operations.

The Riverside Warriors basketball team held a virtual 3-point competition on November 18th where participants streamed shots online in exchange for pledges, drawing local and international viewership.

The Neptune Swimming Association struck a deal on September 30th with a local tech firm to sponsor its championship jerseys, with swimmers' social media directing traffic to the firm's website; marketing chairman is Adam Torres.
The Falcons Baseball Club launched a line of eco-friendly attire with the team's logo on December 5th, spearheaded by creative director Hannah Lee.
The 'Grow-A-Thon' emerged in late 2023; the Cedarwoods Soccer League partnered with local nurseries to sell plantable seeds, led by Michael Thompson.
The Elmtown Hockey Club launched an 'Elite Fans' VIP program on September 20th offering priority seating, signed memorabilia and a chance to be 'Coach for a Day', implemented by Josephine Marks.
The Metroville Track Team, under coach Robert Clark, offered weekend training camps for young runners from October through November for a fee.
The Wildcat Football Club launched 'Wildcat Predicts', a paid game-outcome prediction program with merchandise prizes, managed by analytics head Susan Zhao.
The Bluebirds Softball Team opened an online bakery store with local delivery starting November 1st, led by team parent Olivia Martinez.
The Hilltown Volleyball Club used QR codes on scoreboards and team apps for in-game donations during its championship tournament on December 12th.
Traditional revenue streams are often insufficient to cover rising costs of equipment, travel, and facilities.
